doc_description: A synthetic Solar Microgrid Operations and Maintenance Agreement for North Basin Industrial Park, Nevada, between Westmere Industrial Park Authority (Owner) and Sunhaven Energy Operations Ltd. (Operator), effective 10 March 2027, covering the parties, purpose, asset register, five-year service term, fees, maintenance and response obligations, performance guarantees, safety and cybersecurity controls, insurance, liability, termination, exit assistance, and dispute resolution.

structure.title: Parties, Purpose and Contract Structure
structure.summary: The text is the opening portion of a synthetic Solar Microgrid Operations and Maintenance Agreement for North Basin Industrial Park, Nevada. Section 1 identifies the parties (Westmere Industrial Park Authority as Owner and Sunhaven Energy Operations Ltd. as Operator, effective 10 March 2027), states the purpose (preventive and corrective maintenance, remote monitoring, and performance reporting for listed solar and battery assets), bars the Operator from acting as electricity retailer, requires following the Owner's dispatch protocol, and sets order of precedence among the agreement and Appendices A-C, with amendments controlling only as expressly stated. Section 2 defines the covered assets (7.5 MWdc solar array, 4 MW/16 MWh LFP battery, six MV transformers, supervisory control system), lists exclusions (utility feeder, tenant circuits, third-party telecom), and requires asset record reconciliation within 30 days, escalating discrepancies over 2 percent of critical components.

structure.title: Asset Register and Operating Boundaries
structure.summary: Covers the Solar Microgrid Operations and Maintenance Agreement for North Basin Industrial Park. Asset scope includes a 7.5 MWdc solar PV array, a 4 MW/16 MWh LFP battery system, six medium-voltage transformers, and a site supervisory control system across two fenced yards. Exclusions cover the utility's off-site feeder, Owner tenant circuits, and third-party telecom beyond site demarcation, though incident coordination may be required. Within 30 days of commencement, Operator reconciles serial numbers, warranties, and commissioning records with Owner's register; discrepancies above 2% of critical components require escalation and a corrective plan. The service term runs five years, from 1 May 2027 to 30 April 2032, with an optional two-year extension agreed in writing 90 days before expiry. Mobilization requires safety induction, spare-parts inspection, and remote monitoring handover within 20 Business Days, with Owner providing access credentials and manuals. A joint handover report lists warranty claims, alerts, and deferred work; signing it does not waive EPC or Owner-caused defects.

structure.title: Service Term and Mobilization
structure.summary: The text covers sections 3 and 4 of a Solar Microgrid Operations and Maintenance Agreement for North Basin Industrial Park. Section 3 addresses service term and mobilization: a five-year term from 1 May 2027 to 30 April 2032, with an optional two-year extension by mutual written agreement at least 90 days before expiry; mobilization requirements within 20 Business Days (safety induction, spare-parts inspection, remote monitoring handover) and owner-provided access credentials and manuals; and transition via a joint handover report listing warranty claims, alerts and deferred work orders, without waiving pre-existing EPC or Owner-caused defects. Section 4 covers fees and invoicing: a fixed monthly fee of USD 42,000 including inspections, monitoring and routine maintenance labor; owner approval required for parts over USD 2,500 except safety emergencies; emergency out-of-hours labor at USD 145 per technician-hour; and monthly invoicing in arrears with payment due within 25 days, with late undisputed balances accruing 0.75% monthly interest subject to legal limits.

structure.title: Service Fee, Variable Costs and Invoicing
structure.summary: This excerpt from a Solar Microgrid Operations and Maintenance Agreement for the North Basin Industrial Park covers service fees, variable costs, and invoicing (Section 4), and preventive maintenance and response times (Section 5). Owner pays a fixed monthly fee of USD 42,000 covering routine inspections, remote monitoring, and ordinary preventive maintenance. Replacement parts over USD 2,500 need Owner's written approval unless urgent safety replacement is needed; approved after-hours emergency labor is USD 145 per technician-hour. Operator invoices monthly in arrears, payable within 25 days, with undisputed late balances accruing 0.75% monthly interest up to legal limits. Preventive plans require monthly inverter inspections, quarterly infrared thermography, annual protective relay testing, and six-monthly battery fire-suppression checks, all logged against asset IDs. Critical incidents require remote acknowledgement within 10 minutes and on-site attendance within two hours; High incidents need acknowledgement within 30 minutes. Maintenance deferral is allowed only for weather, permit, or safety reasons, with documented justification, controls, and an Owner-approved revised date.

structure.title: Preventive Maintenance and Response Times
structure.summary: Pages 5-6 of a Solar Microgrid Operations and Maintenance Agreement for the North Basin Industrial Park energy assets portfolio. Section 5 covers preventive maintenance: monthly inverter inspections, quarterly infrared thermography, annual protective relay testing, and six-monthly battery fire-suppression control inspections, all recorded against asset identifiers. It sets incident response times: Critical Incidents (active fire, electrical hazard, or full shutdown) require remote acknowledgement within 10 minutes and on-site attendance within two hours; High Incidents affecting over 20% of generation capacity require acknowledgement within 30 minutes. Maintenance may be deferred only for weather, permit conditions, or safety, with a record stating justification, protective controls, and an Owner-approved revised date. Section 6 covers performance guarantees: 98.5% annual PV availability (excluding grid outages, approved maintenance, and force majeure), no guaranteed battery throughput since Owner controls dispatch, and a fee reduction of 1% per 0.5-point availability shortfall from Operator-controlled causes, capped at 6% of the fixed fee as the sole price remedy.

structure.title: Performance Guarantees and Adjustments
structure.summary: This excerpt from a Solar Microgrid Operations and Maintenance Agreement (North Basin Industrial Park) covers performance guarantees, safety, environmental, and reporting obligations. Section 6 sets a 98.5% annual PV availability guarantee (excluding grid outages, approved maintenance, and force majeure), notes no fixed battery throughput guarantee since the Owner controls dispatch, and provides a fee reduction of 1% per 0.5-point availability shortfall, capped at 6% of the annual fixed fee, as the sole price remedy. Section 7 requires permit-to-work, lockout-tagout, and arc-flash controls, an emergency response plan, and two drills yearly; mandates regulated handling of damaged batteries with licensed transporters; requires reporting of confirmed soil electrolyte releases within one hour; and requires a monthly performance report by the fifth business day, with telemetry retained for 24 months.

structure.title: Safety, Environmental Controls and Reporting
structure.summary: Excerpt from a Solar Microgrid Operations and Maintenance Agreement (North Basin Industrial Park). Section 7 covers safety, environmental controls, and reporting: energized electrical work requires permit-to-work, lockout-tagout, and arc-flash controls; Operator maintains a site-specific emergency response plan with two drills yearly. Damaged battery modules are handled as regulated waste with licensed transporters, and confirmed electrolyte releases to soil must be reported to Owner within one hour. Monthly performance reports (uptime, maintenance, incidents, energy production, open defects) are due by the fifth Business Day, and raw telemetry is retained 24 months. Section 8 covers spares, subcontracting, and cybersecurity: minimum on-site spares of four inverter fan kits, eight DC fuses, and two fire-panel sensors, replenished within 15 Business Days if available; high-voltage subcontracting requires Owner's prior written approval with Operator remaining fully responsible; and named accounts, MFA, and encrypted remote access are required, with credential compromises reported within two hours.

structure.title: Spare Parts, Subcontractors and Cybersecurity
structure.summary: The text covers sections 8 and 9 of a Solar Microgrid Operations and Maintenance Agreement for North Basin Industrial Park. Section 8 addresses critical spares (minimum stock of four inverter cooling fan kits, eight DC string fuses, two fire-panel sensors, replenished within 15 Business Days if available), subcontracting (high-voltage services require Owner's prior written approval, with Operator remaining responsible for subcontractor performance), and cybersecurity (named accounts, multifactor authentication, encrypted remote access, and notification of credential compromise within two hours). Section 9 covers insurance (employer liability as required by law, USD 3 million general liability per occurrence, USD 2 million professional liability per claim), liability cap (100 percent of fees from the prior twelve months, excluding fraud, intentional wrongdoing and negligent bodily injury), and default/termination (30-day cure period for material nonmonetary breaches; termination permitted after three Critical Incident response failures within twelve months, following a written response opportunity).

structure.title: Insurance, Liability and Termination
structure.summary: This pages 9-10 excerpt of a Solar Microgrid Operations and Maintenance Agreement for North Basin Industrial Park covers insurance, liability, termination, exit assistance, notices, and disputes. Operator must carry employer liability insurance, USD 3 million commercial general liability per occurrence, and USD 2 million professional liability per claim. Operator's aggregate liability is capped at 100% of fixed service fees over the prior twelve months, excluding fraud, intentional wrongdoing, and negligent bodily injury. A material nonmonetary breach may be cured within 30 days of notice; three repeated Critical Incident response failures within a rolling twelve months allow termination after a written response opportunity. During the final 45 days, Operator provides exit support materials to the replacement operator; work beyond 40 labor-hours costs USD 95/hour with prior approval. Formal notices require courier or registered mail, with optional email, and helpdesk messages do not count. Nevada law governs, and parties must attempt good-faith mediation in Reno for at least 20 Business Days before ordinary lawsuits.

structure.title: Exit Assistance, Notices and Disputes
structure.summary: This page of a Solar Microgrid Operations and Maintenance Agreement for North Basin Industrial Park covers exit assistance, notices, and disputes. Exit support: during the final 45 days of the term, the Operator provides a live defect register, updated asset inventory, inspection history, and operating credentials to the Owner's replacement operator; support exceeding 40 labor-hours is billed at USD 95/hour with prior written approval. Notice: formal notices must be sent by courier or registered mail to signature-page addresses, with optional email copies; messages only to the operations helpdesk do not count as formal notice. Law and mediation: Nevada law governs, and senior representatives must attempt good-faith mediation in Reno, Nevada, for at least 20 Business Days after a written request before filing an ordinary contractual lawsuit. The page is marked as a synthetic contract, not for execution, and is page 10 of 10.
